content:
### SIT™ Infrastructure Grows Beyondthe Initial Corridor

SIT GroundForce™ launched with a focused strategy: establish territory infrastructure in the highest-value markets of the Chicago–Milwaukee corridor before expanding. The North Shore Chicago and Greater Milwaukee suburbs provided the right combination of homeowner demographics, market density, and growth trajectory to validate the model.

That foundation is now supporting expansion into additional Wisconsin markets — the Fox Valley corridor, the Racine-Kenosha suburban belt, and the Madison area suburbs.

### FoxValley — Appleton, Neenah, Oshkosh, Green Bay Suburbs

The Fox Valley corridor is one of Wisconsin's strongest regional economies and one of its most consistent home improvement markets. Strong manufacturing employment base, high homeownership rates, and a growing suburban population that invests significantly in home maintenance and improvement.

Roofing, HVAC, landscaping, and pest control territory evaluations are now open for select Fox Valley communities. One partner per trade per defined territory — the same model that has driven results in the Milwaukee corridor.

### Racine-KenoshaCorridor — Growing Faster Than The Region

The Racine-Kenosha suburban corridor benefits from its position between two major metros — close enough to Milwaukee and Chicago to attract professional-class residents, far enough to offer the space and homeownership rates that support high home service investment.

This corridor has historically been underserved by structured territory programs despite having homeowner demographics that align well with the GroundForce™ model. Current evaluations are open across multiple trade categories.

### Madison Area Suburbs — University Town Meets Affluent Suburban Market

The Madison area suburbs —Middleton, Waunakee, Fitchburg, Sun Prairie, and Verona — combine the purchasing power of a professional and academic workforce with the residential density of a growing suburban market.

Home improvement investment in these communities is strong and growing. Territory availability across roofing, HVAC, window, and landscaping categories is currently open for evaluation.
